sentences: In the 1909 World Series the Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Detroit Tigers 8-0 at Bennett Park in Detroit.
Rookie Babe Adams threw a six-hit shutout for his third win of the series in 1909.
The Boston Red Sox beat the New York Giants 3-2 in 10 innings at Fenway Park in Boston in 1912.
The 1912 decisive contest was game eight, because game two had ended in a tie.
The Washington Senators beat the New York Giants 4-3 in 12 innings at Griffith Stadium in Washington, D.C. in 1924.
The 1924 game was the longest game seven in innings.
In the 12th inning of the 1924 game, Muddy Ruel doubled after a dropped foul popfly by Giants catcher Hank Gowdy.
Ruel scored on a game-winning RBI double by Earl McNeely.
The Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Washington Senators 9-7 at Forbes Field in Pittsburgh in 1925.
Pittsburgh became the first team in a best-of-seven series to win the series after trailing three games to one.
The St. Louis Cardinals beat the New York Yankees 3-2 at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, New York City in 1926.
Grover Cleveland Alexander struck out Tony Lazzeri with the bases loaded to end the seventh inning and preserve the Cardinals lead in 1926.
Two innings later in 1926, Babe Ruth was caught stealing to end the World Series.
The St. Louis Cardinals beat the Philadelphia Athletics 4-2 in St. Louis, Missouri in 1931.
The 1931 game was the last postseason game for the Athletics while they were based in Philadelphia.
The St. Louis Cardinals beat the Detroit Tigers 11-0 at Navin Field in Detroit in 1934.
Dizzy Dean earned his second win of the 1934 Series with a six-hit shutout on one day of rest.
The 1934 win gave the Cardinals the title.
The Cincinnati Reds beat the Detroit Tigers 2-1 at Crosley Field in Cincinnati in 1940.
The 1940 game was over in a snappy 1 hour 47 minutes.
A sacrifice bunt and a sacrifice fly scored the winning runs in the 1940 game.
The Detroit Tigers beat the Chicago Cubs 9-3 at Wrigley Field in Chicago in 1945.
The Chicago Cubs' 1945 appearance was their last World Series appearance until 2016.
The 1945 entry includes a see-also reference to the Curse of the Billy Goat.
The St. Louis Cardinals beat the Boston Red Sox 4-3 at Sportsman's Park III in St. Louis, Missouri in 1946.
Enos Slaughter's famous mad dash scored the deciding run to win the 1946 game and the series.
The New York Yankees beat the Brooklyn Dodgers 5-2 at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, New York City in 1947.
The 1947 Series featured Cookie Lavagetto's pinch-hit that spoiled Bill Bevens' no-hit bid.
The 1947 Series featured Al Gionfriddo's catch that robbed Joe DiMaggio of a home run.
The New York Yankees beat the Brooklyn Dodgers 4-2 at Ebbets Field in Brooklyn, New York City in 1952.
Billy Martin's game-saving infield catch in 1952 preserved the Yankees lead and helped win the game and the series.
The Brooklyn Dodgers beat the New York Yankees 2-0 at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, New York City in 1955.
The 1955 championship was the Dodgers' only championship in Brooklyn.
In the 1955 series the home team won all games except game seven.
The New York Yankees beat the Brooklyn Dodgers 9-0 at Ebbets Field in Brooklyn, New York City in 1956.
The 1956 game was Jackie Robinson's final Major League game.
The 1956 game was the last postseason game at Ebbets Field.
The 1956 game was the Dodgers' last postseason game before moving to Los Angeles.
In the 1956 series the home team won all games except game seven.
The Milwaukee Braves beat the New York Yankees 5-0 at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, New York City in 1957.
The 1957 championship was the Braves' only championship in Milwaukee.
The New York Yankees beat the Milwaukee Braves 6-2 at County Stadium in Milwaukee in 1958.
The 1958 Yankees won their 18th World Series title after being down three games to one.
The 1958 game was the Braves' last postseason game in Milwaukee.
The Pittsburgh Pirates beat the New York Yankees 10-9 at Forbes Field in Pittsburgh in 1960.
Bill Mazeroski hit the walk-off home run in 1960 to win the championship for the Pirates.
The 1960 game was the last postseason game in Forbes Field.
The 1960 game was the last postseason game for Yankees manager Casey Stengel.
The 1960 game was the highest scoring game seven.
The New York Yankees beat the San Francisco Giants 1-0 at Candlestick Park in San Francisco in 1962.
With runners on second and third and two outs in 1962, Willie McCovey's line drive to Bobby Richardson ended the game.
The 1962 game was the first game seven to end with a 1-0 score.
The St. Louis Cardinals beat the New York Yankees 7-5 at Busch Stadium I in St. Louis, Missouri in 1964.
The 1964 Yankees' appearance was their last World Series appearance until 1976.
The 1964 game was the last postseason game at Busch Stadium I.
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Minnesota Twins 2-0 at Metropolitan Stadium in Bloomington, Minnesota in 1965.
Sandy Koufax pitched through immense pain on two days' rest in 1965 and threw a 3-hit shutout.
Sandy Koufax won the 1965 Series and was named World Series MVP.
In the 1965 series the home team won all games except game seven.
The St. Louis Cardinals beat the Boston Red Sox 7-2 at Fenway Park in Boston in 1967.
Bob Gibson won his third game of the 1967 Series and also hit a home run.
The Detroit Tigers beat the St. Louis Cardinals 4-1 at Busch Stadium II in St. Louis, Missouri in 1968.
Mickey Lolich outdueled Bob Gibson in the 1968 game.
The Detroit Tigers rallied from a 3-1 deficit to win the 1968 series.
The 1968 game was the first game seven loss by the Cardinals in the World Series.
The Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Baltimore Orioles 2-1 at Memorial Stadium in Baltimore in 1971.
In the 1971 series the home team won all games except game seven.
The Oakland Athletics beat the Cincinnati Reds 3-2 at Riverfront Stadium in Cincinnati in 1972.
The 1972 championship was the first championship for the Athletics in Oakland.
The Athletics were the last American League team to win a World Series game seven on the road until 2017.
The Oakland Athletics beat the New York Mets 5-2 at the Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum in Oakland, California in 1973.
Bert Campaneris and Reggie Jackson hit the only Oakland home runs in the 1973 game, setting the tone for victory and the series.
The Cincinnati Reds beat the Boston Red Sox 4-3 at Fenway Park in Boston in 1973.
The 1973 Reds game came one night after Carlton Fisk's famous home run.
The Cincinnati Reds rebounded to take the 1973 Series.
The Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Baltimore Orioles 4-1 at Memorial Stadium in Baltimore in 1979.
The Pittsburgh Pirates, powered by NLCS and World Series MVP Willie Stargell, rallied from a 3-1 deficit to win the 1979 series.
The Pittsburgh Pirates were the last team to win a road game seven until 2014.
The St. Louis Cardinals beat the Milwaukee Brewers 6-3 at Busch Stadium II in St. Louis, Missouri in 1982.
Joaquin Andujar earned his second win of the 1982 Series.
Bruce Sutter earned his second save of the 1982 Series.
The Kansas City Royals beat the St. Louis Cardinals 11-0 at Royals Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri in 1985.
The 1985 Series was the second World Series held entirely in the state of Missouri.
The Royals also won the 1985 American League Championship Series in seven games.
The Royals became the first team to win the World Series after losing the first two games at home.

The Royals were the last team to come back from 3-1 down to win a title in any of the five major men's professional sports leagues until the Cleveland Cavaliers won the 2016 NBA Finals after trailing 3-1.
The 1985 Royals were the last team to win a World Series after trailing 3-1 until the Cubs did so in 2016.
The New York Mets beat the Boston Red Sox 8-5 at Shea Stadium in Flushing, Queens, New York in 1986.
The 1986 Mets became the first team to be one strike away from elimination and come back to win the series.
The 1986 Mets became the second team to win the series after losing the first two games at home.
The Minnesota Twins beat the St. Louis Cardinals 4-2 at the Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome in Minneapolis in the entry listed without a year.
The home team won all seven games of that series for the first time in MLB history.
The Minnesota Twins beat the Atlanta Braves 1-0 in 10 innings at the Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome in Minneapolis in 1991.
Like in 1987, the home team won all games of the 1991 series.
The Twins won the 1991 game in the bottom of the 10th on a walk-off single by Gene Larkin, scoring Dan Gladden after scoreless innings of play.
Jack Morris went all ten innings for the Twins in 1991 and was named Series MVP.
Kirby Puckett hit a famous walk-off home run in the bottom of the 11th inning of the previous night's game to force the decisive 1991 game.
The Florida Marlins beat the Cleveland Indians 3-2 in 11 innings at Pro Player Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida in 1997.
Florida became the first wild card team to win the World Series in 1997.
The Marlins rallied for one run in the bottom of the ninth in 1997 to tie the game.
The Marlins won the 1997 game in the 11th inning on an Edgar Renteria RBI single off Charles Nagy.
The Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 3-2 at Bank One Ballpark in Phoenix, Arizona in 2001.
Arizona became the fastest expansion team to win the World Series in 2001.
Arizona rallied for two runs in the bottom of the ninth in 2001 for a come-from-behind win.
Luis Gonzalez hit the winning RBI single off closer Mariano Rivera in 2001.
The home team won every game of the 2001 series.
The Anaheim Angels beat the San Francisco Giants 4-1 at Edison International Field in Anaheim, California in 2002.
Both 2002 World Series teams were wild card entrants into the playoffs.
John Lackey became the second rookie pitcher to win a World Series game seven in 2002.
The St. Louis Cardinals beat the Texas Rangers 6-2 at Busch Stadium in St. Louis, Missouri in 2011.
The Cardinals became the second team to be one strike away from elimination and come back to win the series, which they did twice.
Like the 1991 series, a walk-off home run in the bottom of the 11th inning of game six forced the 2011 decisive game, with David Freese providing the firepower.
The 2011 game seven was the most recent game seven won by the home team.
The San Francisco Giants beat the Kansas City Royals 3-2 at Kauffman Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri in 2014.
Like in 2002, both 2014 World Series teams were wild card entrants into the playoffs.
The Giants became the first NL team to win a game seven on the road since 1979.
Madison Bumgarner was the NLCS MVP and eventual World Series MVP in 2014.
Madison Bumgarner is normally a starter but pitched five scoreless innings of relief on two days' rest in 2014.
The 2014 relief pitching saved the Giants' third title in five years.
The Chicago Cubs beat the Cleveland Indians 8-7 in 10 innings at Progressive Field in Cleveland, Ohio in 2016.
The 2016 win was the Chicago Cubs' first World Series win since 1908.
The 2016 game was played between the two teams with the longest active championship droughts.
The Cubs are the first Major League Baseball team to come back to win the World Series from a 3-1 series deficit since the 1985 Royals.
The 2016 game seven was the most recent World Series game seven to be decided in extra innings.
The 2016 game seven was the first extra innings game seven to be won by the road team.
The Houston Astros beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 5-1 at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles in 2017.
The 2017 series was the first instance of back-to-back game sevens since 2001-2002.
The 2017 championship was the first World Series championship for the Astros.
The Astros became the first AL team to win a World Series game 7 on the road since 1972.
The Astros became the second team to win two winner-take-all game sevens in the same postseason since the Kansas City Royals in 1985.

In most of the world, speed limit signs display the limit within a red circle.
The red circle design follows the style set out by the Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals.
The United States and Canada are exceptions to the Vienna Convention style.
All countries worldwide, except the United Kingdom and United States, use metric speed limits in kilometres per hour.
Metric signs are optional in the United States, though less commonly seen.
Samoa uses both metric and imperial units for speed limits.
In Ontario, Canada, the type, location, and frequency of speed limit signs are covered by regulation 615 of the Ontario Highway Traffic Act.
Dragon Ball Z, Japanese title Doragon Boru Zetto, is commonly abbreviated as DBZ.
Dragon Ball Z is the long-running anime sequel to the Dragon Ball TV series.
Dragon Ball Z is adapted from the final twenty-six volumes of the Dragon Ball manga written by Akira Toriyama.
The Dragon Ball Z manga portion debuted in Weekly Shonen Jump on October 4, 1988.
The Dragon Ball Z manga portion lasted until 1995.
The Dragon Ball Z anime premiered in Japan on Fuji Television on April 26, 1989.
The Dragon Ball Z anime took over its predecessor's time slot.
The Dragon Ball Z anime ran until its end on January 31, 1996.
The Dragon Ball Z anime lasted 291 episodes in Japan.
The Dragon Ball Z anime originally lasted 276 episodes in the United States.
All 291 Dragon Ball Z episodes were later broadcast.
All 291 episodes were later broadcast after content from the first 67 episodes was restored.
The Urdu lyrics of the anthem are presented in Urdu script.
The transliteration of the lyrics follows the ALA-LC romanization system.
The first line of the Urdu lyrics, Pak sarzamin shad bad, asks that the holy land stay glad.
The poetical translation reads May the holy land stay glad and Beautious realm stay glad.
The literal translation reads Blessed be the sacred land and happy be the bounteous realm.
The lyrics address the Land of Pakistan as the sign of high resolve.
The lyrics call the land the citadel of faith.
The second stanza refers to the order of the holy land and the power of the fraternity of the populace.
The second stanza names the nation, the country, and the state, and asks that they shine in everlasting glory.
The second stanza describes the cherished goal as glad.
The third stanza refers to the flag with the star and crescent.
The third stanza calls the leader of progress and ascent a rahbar.
The third stanza calls the past's interpreter and the present's pride the dragoman of the past and the glory of the present.
The third stanza calls the soul of the future the inspiration for the future.
The final line refers to the shadow of God, the Glorious and Mighty.

The states were preexisting political entities, so the U.S. Constitution did not need to define or explain federalism in any one section.
The U.S. Constitution often mentions the rights and responsibilities of state governments and state officials in relation to the federal government.
The federal government has express powers, also called enumerated powers, which are spelled out in the Constitution.
The express powers include the right to levy taxes, declare war, and regulate interstate and foreign commerce.
The Necessary and Proper Clause gives the federal government the implied power to pass any law necessary and proper for executing its express powers.
Reserved powers are reserved to the people or the states.
The Supreme Court decision in McCulloch v. Maryland (1819) significantly expanded the power delegated to the federal government.
Amendments to the Constitution following the Civil War significantly expanded the power delegated to the federal government.
Some later amendments also expanded the power delegated to the federal government.
The overall claim of the Civil War was that the states were legally subject to the final dictates of the federal government.
